title: Phenological Changes in Pollination Pals
text:
With warming temperatures due to anthropogenic climate change, migrating birds are starting to move back to their breeding grounds earlier each year [1]. Along with this, flowers that certain migrating birds, like Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (Archilochus colubris), feed on may be changing their flowering times due to climate change [2].



Ruby-throated Hummingbird [3]


I want to investigate how the Ruby-throated Hummingbird has been shifting its spring migration patterns at varying latitudes, and how the appearances of two spring ephemeral species it prefers to feed on during this migration, Red Buckeye (Aesculus pavia) and Red Columbine (Aquilegia canadensis), has changed (or not changed) over the past 10* years at varying latitudes [4].
*My maps and graphs are from 2014 to 2025 to account for any incomplete datasets from 2025






Red Columbine [5]







Red Buckeye [6]





I predict that Ruby-throated Hummingbirds are migrating back to their breeding grounds earlier each year, and that they are arriving at higher latitudes increasingly earlier than lower latitudes. Additionally, I suppose that the first sightings of these preferred flowers will be earlier at higher latitudes and later at lower latitudes compared to previous years. So, as Ruby-throated Hummingbirds migrate back earlier, these flowers may not be available at lower latitudes for them to feed on.

all_flower <- all_flower %>%
  mutate(observed_on = parse_date_time(observed_on, orders = c("mdy", "ydm", "dmy"))) %>% # Standardizes date formats

section: 5. Flowers: Calculate Means of Early Period (2005-2013)
text:
5. Flowers: Calculate Means of Early Period (2005-2013)

Found the mean date of first flower sightings from 2005 to 2013 and from March to May (when these flowers’ bloom times overlap) [7,8]
Separated sightings into 3 bands of latitude to account for difference in average flowering times in across their range (grouped latitudes had similar “year_day” averages)



Code
fl_early <- all_flower %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5))

fl_early_all <- fl_early %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,36,42,48), labels = c("30-36", "36-42", "42-48"))) %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) 
  
fl_means <- fl_early_all %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  summarise(mean) %>%
  rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Flowering Day Mean" = "mean")

selected_fl <- fl_means[c(1, 25, 39), ]

kable(selected_fl, format = "pipe", caption = '<span style="color: darkred;">2005-2013 Flowering Time Means</span>')

title: Phenological Changes in Pollination Pals
section: 6. Flowers: Calculate Means and Difference From 2014-2025 to 2005-2013
text:
6. Flowers: Calculate Means and Difference From 2014-2025 to 2005-2013

Added a column (mean0013) based on table of flowering means by latitude
Used 6 bands of latitude for more specific analysis
Created a “difference” column, showing the difference in days of arrival between the early and current average using mean - mean0013
Bound all of these bands into one dataset for plotting



Code
fl_new <- all_flower %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) %>%
  mutate(mean0513 = 
         case_when(
         latitude > 30 & latitude < 33 ~ 81.95652,
         latitude > 33 & latitude < 36 ~ 81.95652,
         latitude > 36 & latitude < 39 ~ 99.73333,
         latitude > 39 & latitude < 42 ~ 99.73333,
         latitude > 42 & latitude < 45 ~ 114.30769,
         latitude > 45 & latitude < 48 ~ 114.30769))

fl_new_all <- fl_new %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48))) %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(difference = mean-mean0513) %>%
  drop_na(difference)

fl_new_difference <- fl_new_all %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", "36-39", "39-42","42-45", "45-48"))) %>%
  group_by(difference) %>%
  select(latbin, difference) %>%
  rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Difference in Ruby-throat Arrival Dates" = "difference") 

fl_new_difference <- fl_new_difference[c(1, 895, 222, 1425, 2656, 4115), ]

# dplyr and lubridate used to standardize and add columns from dates

all_flower <- all_flower %>%
  mutate(observed_on = parse_date_time(observed_on, orders = c("mdy", "ydm", "dmy"))) %>% # Standardizes date formats
  mutate(year = year(observed_on)) %>% # Pulls year from date
  mutate(year_day = yday(observed_on)) %>% # Puts date into day out of 365
  mutate(month = month(observed_on)) # Pulls month from date

title: Phenological Changes in Pollination Pals

5.

Flowers: Calculate Means of Early Period (2005-2013)

Found the mean date of first flower sightings from 2005 to 2013 and from March to May (when these flowers’ bloom times overlap) [7, 8]
Separated sightings into 3 bands of latitude to account for difference in average flowering times across their range (grouped by latitudes with similar “year_day” averages)



Code
fl_early <- all_flower %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5))

fl_early_all <- fl_early %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,36,42,48), labels = c("30-36", "36-42", "42-48"))) %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) 
  
fl_means <- fl_early_all %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  summarise(mean) %>%
  rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Flowering Day Mean" = "mean")

#One row for each latitude band mean selected
selected_fl <- fl_means[c(1, 25, 39), ]

#Table to show early period flowering times based on latitude bands

title: Phenological Changes in Pollination Pals
text:
6.

Flowers: Calculate Means and Difference From 2014-2025 to 2005-2013

Added a column (mean0513) based on “2005-2013 Flowering Time Means” table and assigned by corresponding latitudes
Used 6 bands of latitude for more specific analysis
Created a “difference” column, showing the difference in days of arrival between the early and current average using mean - mean0513
Bound all of these bands into one dataset for plotting



Code
fl_new <- all_flower %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) %>%
  mutate(mean0513 = 
         case_when(
         latitude > 30 & latitude < 33 ~ 81.95652,
         latitude > 33 & latitude < 36 ~ 81.95652,
         latitude > 36 & latitude < 39 ~ 99.73333,
         latitude > 39 & latitude < 42 ~ 99.73333,
         latitude > 42 & latitude < 45 ~ 114.30769,
         latitude > 45 & latitude < 48 ~ 114.30769))

fl_new_all <- fl_new %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48))) %>%
  group_by(latbin) %>%
  mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(difference = mean-mean0513) %>%
  drop_na(difference)

fl_new_difference <- fl_new_all %>%
  mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", "36-39", "39-42","42-45", "45-48"))) %>%
  group_by(difference) %>%
  select(latbin, difference) %>%
  rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Difference in Ruby-throat Arrival Dates" = "difference") 

#Selected 1 row for each latitude band difference
fl_new_difference <- fl_new_difference[c(1, 895, 222, 1425, 2656, 4115), ]

Or:
Download the Ruby-throated Hummingbird data from eBird by visiting: https://media.ebird.org/catalog?birdOnly=true&taxonCode=rthhum, filter by year (I did this in two separate actions [1995-2021 and 2022-2025] to ensure I could download all of the data), filter by location (United States), and download as a csv.
